description: Reports the state of a specification package: its lifecycle status, whether it validates, every task with its state and whether it is ready, the next task to work on, the lifecycle moves allowed from its status, and the packages it depends on and that depend on it. With --validate, the format's full verdict on the package; with --list, every package under the spec root. It changes nothing. spec writes a package from an idea, specr renders one, speca reports its state.

input.description: Exactly one reference to a spec package: a path to its directory or to a file inside it, or a directory name, spec number or spec name under the spec root (16_indexed_code_search, 16, indexed_code_search). None with --list.

all.description: with --list, also list the packages under archive/, marked archived

dir.description: the repository the spec root and a relative reference are resolved against

list.description: list every package under the spec root, in number order, each with its status, whether it validates, its task counts and its next task; takes no input

specs-dir.description: where NN_name packages live; default <dir>/.specs or $AF_SPEC_DIR

validate.description: give the format's full verdict on the package: the schemas, the cross-file rules C1 to C11 and the cross-spec rules that concern it, each finding naming its rule; a package that does not validate is still a successful call

tool.description: the command that wrote this envelope

ok.description: true only when the command did the whole job it was asked to do; never true beside a non-zero exit_code or an error

status.description: the outcome in words, derived from exit_code: done (0), failed (1) or usage (2)

exit_code.description: the process exit code: 0 done, 1 failed, 2 usage error

summary.description: one sentence on the outcome, at most 200 characters

error.description: what failed and where; present exactly when ok is false

category.description: the kind of failure, which says whether re-running could help; an open set

retryable.description: whether re-running the identical command could succeed

resumable.description: whether re-running the same input continues the work rather than starting it over

fix_hint.description: a mechanical remedy, where one is known

env.description: the environment variables, one of which supplies what is missing

valid.description: the values the flag accepts here

current.description: the flag's value on this run

warnings.description: what went differently than intended without stopping the run

code.description: a stable code naming the cause; an open set

severity.description: high when the result is not quite what it appears to be, low when informational

spec_dir.description: the package directory, relative to --dir when inside it, absolute otherwise; runnable as the input of specr and speca; the report and the verdict

spec_id.description: the spec id, from the PRD frontmatter; the report and the verdict

spec_name.description: the spec name, from the PRD frontmatter; the report and the verdict

title.description: the spec title, from the PRD frontmatter; the report and the verdict

status.description: the package's lifecycle status: draft, active, sealed, superseded or archived; the report and the verdict

created_at.description: when the package was created, RFC 3339, from the PRD frontmatter; the report and the verdict

updated_at.description: when the package was last updated, RFC 3339, from the PRD frontmatter; the report and the verdict

intent_hash.description: the SHA-256 of the PRD's ## Intent section, recorded when the package was activated; absent while unset

supersedes.description: the spec ids this package supersedes; absent when it supersedes none

tags.description: the package's tags, from the PRD frontmatter; absent when it has none

valid.description: whether the package validates. In the report, its own verdict, from the schemas and the cross-file rules C1 to C11; with --validate, the combined verdict: true exactly when no error was kept from the package's own rules or the cross-spec rules. Absent under --list, where each entry holds its own

failing_rules.description: the rules the package's errors break, in order of first appearance; the report only, and present only when valid is false

intent_drift.description: true when the package is active, has an intent_hash, and its PRD's ## Intent section no longer hashes to it or is gone, so that every save is refused; absent otherwise; the report and the verdict

tasks.description: every task of the plan, in order, with its state and whether it is ready; [] when the plan has none; the report only

id.description: the task id, as --task takes it

kind.description: implement, or integration for the plan's last task

optional.description: true when the task may be skipped

depends_on.description: the tasks that must be done first

ready.description: true for a pending task whose dependencies are all done; absent otherwise

task_counts.description: the tasks counted by state, and their total; the report only

in_progress.description: the tasks that are in progress

total.description: every task of the plan: the four counts added

next_task.description: the task to work on now: the first in_progress task, else the first ready one; absent when there is none; the report only

id.description: the task id, as --task takes it

kind.description: implement, or integration for the plan's last task

optional.description: true when the task may be skipped

depends_on.description: the tasks that must be done first

ready.description: true for a pending task whose dependencies are all done; absent otherwise

allowed_status.description: the lifecycle states the package may move to from its status, in the order draft, active, sealed, superseded, archived; [] for a terminal status; the report only

depends_on.description: the spec ids in the package's own tasks.json dependencies, in file order without duplicates; [] when it has none; the report only

dependents.description: the spec ids of the other packages under the spec root that depend on this one, sorted without duplicates; [] when none does, absent when the spec root could not be read; the report only

validation.description: the format's verdict: valid, error_count, warning_count, and every error and warning with its check (the rule), artifact, entity and message; the package's own findings first, then the cross-spec findings that concern it; --validate only

traceability.description: the derived coverage: criteria_covered, criteria_uncovered, paths_covered, paths_uncovered and tests_unowned; --validate only

packages.description: one entry for every package under the spec root in number order, then with --all those under archive/; [] when there are none; --list only

spec_dir.description: the package directory, relative to --dir when inside it, absolute otherwise; runnable as the input of specr and speca

spec_id.description: the spec id, from the PRD frontmatter; absent when the package did not load

spec_name.description: the spec name, from the PRD frontmatter; absent when the package did not load

title.description: the spec title, from the PRD frontmatter; absent when the package did not load

status.description: the package's lifecycle status; absent when the package did not load

valid.description: whether the package validates on its own rules; absent when the package did not load

task_counts.description: the tasks counted by state; absent when the package did not load

in_progress.description: the tasks that are in progress

total.description: every task of the plan: the four counts added

next_task.description: the task to work on now: the first in_progress task, else the first ready one; absent when there is none

id.description: the task id, as --task takes it

kind.description: implement, or integration for the plan's last task

optional.description: true when the task may be skipped

depends_on.description: the tasks that must be done first

ready.description: true for a pending task whose dependencies are all done; absent otherwise

archived.description: true for a package listed from archive/, whatever its status (a superseded package there is archived: true with status superseded); absent otherwise

load_error.description: why the package did not load, in the library's words; present exactly when it did not, and then the only field besides spec_dir

artifacts.description: what the run produced, read off facts the command holds

kind.description: what the entry is; its other fields are the ones of its kind

dry_run.description: true when it would have been written but for --dry-run

next.description: the invocations a caller would plausibly make next

flags.description: the flags to add, each value its own element

why.description: why a caller would run it

duration_ms.description: wall-clock time of the run, in milliseconds

started_at.description: when the run started, RFC 3339 in UTC

exit_codes.0: reported: the state of a package, its verdict (a package that does not validate is reported too), or the list of packages
exit_codes.1: failed: the package could not be loaded, or the spec root --list reads could not be read; the stage is named in error
exit_codes.2: usage error: the reference names no package or two, two operations in one call, or a flag that cannot hold; nothing was read
